raw_case_text: This 26-year old Zimbabwean-born Caucasian patient had lived in the UK for four years and reported having malaria 3 times before moving to the UK. The patient presented with circulating P. falciparum trophozoites and schizonts at a parasitaemia of 1.3% following a visit to Mozambique (Mapute/Tete) for a period of three weeks, during which no chemoprophylaxis or treatment was taken. A single pre-treatment blood sample was analysed.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 26-year-old Zimbabwean-born Caucasian patient presented with acute malaria following a 3-week visit to Mozambique.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient developed clinical Plasmodium falciparum infection after returning to the UK from a 3-week trip to Maputo and Tete, Mozambique.
subjective.past_medical_history: Born in Zimbabwe, resided in the UK for 4 years; history of 3 prior malaria episodes before moving to the UK. Took no antimalarial chemoprophylaxis or treatment during the 3-week visit to Mozambique.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Imported uncomplicated polyclonal Plasmodium falciparum malaria (isolate OX001/PL0001). Confirmed by peripheral blood microscopy showing circulating P. falciparum trophozoites and schizonts at 1.3% parasitemia, with massively parallel sequencing (MPS) and nested PCR of pfmsp1/pfmsp2 demonstrating a polyclonal infection harboring pfef2 amplification, a 587 bp deletion in pfrbp2b, a novel T496I substitution plus 86Y/1246Y mutations in pfmdr1, and the triple-mutant IRNI haplotype in pfdhfr.
